games.title: Bagh Chal (Tiger Game)
games.description: A traditional strategic board game representing tigers hunting goats. Four tigers attempt to capture goats while twenty goats try to trap the tigers. Deeply rooted in Nepali culture.
equipment: Wooden board with cross and diagonal lines
howToPlay: Step 1: The board features a cross with diagonal lines forming intersections.
Step 2: One player controls 4 tigers placed at the board's corners.
Step 3: The other player controls 20 goats, initially placed off-board.
Step 4: Goats are placed one by one on any empty intersection.
Step 5: Tigers move along lines, capturing goats by jumping over them to empty spaces.
Step 6: Goats cannot capture but aim to surround and trap tigers so they cannot move.
Step 7: Tigers win by capturing 5 goats or reducing goats' mobility.
Step 8: Goats win by completely immobilizing all tigers.
Step 9: The game requires deep strategic thinking and forward planning.
Step 10: Matches can last from 30 minutes to several hours.

games.title: Chyangma
games.description: A traditional game played in mountain regions using woven bamboo rings. Players throw rings at a target, competing for accuracy.
howToPlay: Step 1: Create rings by weaving bamboo strips into circles.
Step 2: Place a stake or peg in the ground at a distance.
Step 3: Players take turns throwing rings toward the stake.
Step 4: Points awarded for rings that land on or near the stake.
Step 5: Rings that encircle the stake score highest points.
Step 6: Multiple rounds are played with cumulative scoring.
Step 7: Players develop throwing accuracy and touch.
Step 8: The game uses locally available materials.
Step 9: Often played during leisure time in mountain villages.
Step 10: Winners receive recognition within the community.

games.title: Dandi Biyo
games.description: Considered the oldest game in Nepal, similar to Gilli Danda. Players use a long stick (dandi) to hit a smaller tapered stick (biyo) and compete for distance.
howToPlay: Step 1: A small hole is dug in the ground or a circle drawn.
Step 2: Place the biyo across the hole with one end raised.
Step 3: Use the dandi to flick the biyo into the air.
Step 4: Strike the airborne biyo with the dandi to hit it far.
Step 5: Fielders try to catch the biyo before it lands.
Step 6: If caught, batter is out; if not, measure distance using dandi lengths.
Step 7: Batter scores points equal to number of dandi lengths.
Step 8: Players take turns batting and fielding.
Step 9: Player with highest total distance wins.
Step 10: Considered the national traditional game of Nepal.

games.title: Dhyakki (Hopscotch)
games.description: Nepali version of hopscotch, primarily played by girls. Players hop through numbered boxes while kicking a flat stone, testing balance and precision.
equipment: Chalk or stick to draw boxes
howToPlay: Step 1: Draw a hopscotch grid with numbered boxes on the ground.
Step 2: Players toss a flat stone into the first box.
Step 3: Hop on one foot through the boxes, avoiding the box with the stone.
Step 4: Kick the stone to the next box while hopping.
Step 5: Continue until reaching the end and turn back.
Step 6: If successful, toss stone to next box and repeat.
Step 7: Player loses turn if stone lands on a line, both feet touch ground, or balance is lost.
Step 8: Player who completes all boxes first wins.
Step 9: Advanced players add complex patterns and faster movements.
Step 10: Singing often accompanies the game.

games.title: Kabbadi (Nepali Style)
games.description: Nepali variation of kabaddi with slightly modified rules, particularly popular in rural areas and school competitions.
howToPlay: Step 1: Similar to standard kabaddi with minor rule variations by region.
Step 2: Two teams of seven occupy opposite halves of a rectangular court.
Step 3: One team sends a raider into opponent's half chanting 'kabbadi'.
Step 4: Raider attempts to tag defenders and return to their half.
Step 5: Defenders try to tackle the raider.
Step 6: Points scored for successful tags.
Step 7: Teams alternate raiders throughout the game.
Step 8: Local rules may vary regarding breathing and tackling.
Step 9: Popular in both rural and urban areas.
Step 10: Featured in school-level competitions.

games.title: Surung (Tunnel Game)
games.description: A traditional game where players form human tunnels by bending over in lines, while others crawl through. Tests agility and teamwork.
howToPlay: Step 1: Players divide into two teams.
Step 2: One team forms a tunnel by bending forward and placing hands on knees in a line.
Step 3: The other team takes turns crawling through the tunnel.
Step 4: After all players have crawled through, teams switch roles.
Step 5: The team that completes crawling faster wins.
Step 6: Variations include obstacles and timed challenges.
Step 7: Players must maintain tunnel formation throughout.
Step 8: Game builds teamwork and physical coordination.
Step 9: Popular during school sports days.
Step 10: Requires no equipment, making it accessible to all.
